sections.briefing_title_en: Science and Tech: New Findings From Lunar Radiation to Immune Sensing
sections.briefing_summary_en: This edition covers two subsections, space energy and robotics, and scientific research. Researchers used chip-manufacturing techniques to suppress lithium buildup, potentially enabling smaller, more durable EV batteries; scientists outlined seven stages that meteors undergo, with melting and violent fragmentation rather than simple burn-up; and NASA's Artemis I mission found cosmic radiation near the Moon higher than in Earth orbit but lower than expected, while revealing how radiation passes through the human body. In research, a team generated X-rays at higher energies than conventional theory predicts; a new study proposed that Northern Hemisphere ice-sheet expansion could affect conditions near Antarctica through southward-moving ocean waters and help drive ice ages; a small group of brain cells was found to prevent dangerous blood pressure swings; and T cells were found to sense tissue stiffness and use it to influence memory-cell development.
